lanes.lane: A — Reading order without a tree (spec #4) + the Detect-Order-Construct paper
lanes.measured_on_specimen: Ran a self-written ~55-line recursive XY-cut (xycut_probe.py, CPU-only, pymupdf+re+difflib, no torch) over pymupdf get_text("dict") block bboxes — the same shape J24's marker_blocks.py persists — on the two specimens that actually carry a structure-tree ground truth: Well-Tagged-PDF-WTPDF-1.0.pdf (57pp) and ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.pdf (60pp), C:/Users/Bndit/Downloads/. Reused probe_k_order.py's declared_frags()/geom_frags() verbatim as ground truth and Marker-baseline proxy rather than re-deriving a parallel methodology. Negative control run and Verified: (1) determinism self-compare True; (2) planted two-column synthetic page (full-height contiguous columns, 50pt gutter, column-interleaved input) — naive y-sort wrong, xy_cut correct — this IS the regression test. Measured v1 (plain XY-cut): 55/57 and 59/60 pages disagree with declared order (far worse than baseline's 2/57, 15/60). Diagnosed the cause (diag.py): a running footer, geometrically at page-bottom but content-stream-first, breaks pure-geometry sorting. Built v2 (margin-band header/footer excluded from the cut): WTPDF collapses to 2/57 (matches baseline exactly); ISO improves to 18/60 (still worse than baseline's 15/60). Computed the number that actually answers the spec (xycut_v3_net.py): on the pages where Marker's own stream-order baseline is already wrong, v2 XY-cut fixes 0/2 (WTPDF) and 0/15 (ISO), while breaking 3 ISO pages the baseline got right. Diagnosed those residual failures (diag_p0.py): they are cover/title pages with anomalous bboxes (one block at y0=-20.7), not multi-column body text — the algorithm's actual target case was never exercised by either ground-truthed specimen. Also read marker/processors/order.py, marker/builders/layout.py, and surya/layout/__init__.py directly to correct an assumption in the brief: Marker's current "geometric order" is actually pdftext span-order (stream order), not geometry — surya's layout position field (an autoregressive decode index) is only used as a fallback for spanless blocks.
lanes.residue: Did not measure PdfPig's DocstrumBoundingBoxes or UnsupervisedReadingOrderDetector (interval-algebra) algorithms this session — only ported and measured RecursiveXYCut. Those two are plausible candidates for the cover-page/anomalous-bbox failure mode found (nearest-neighbour and interval-algebra don't assume axis-aligned gaps the way XY-cut does), flagged MEASURE_NEXT, not ruled out. The PdfPig wiki content itself came back as an AI-summarized WebFetch, not hand-parsed raw wiki markdown — tagged Observed, not independently re-verified against source text. Could not test XY-cut's actual target case (genuine multi-column running body text) against any ground truth at all: only 19/4,307 (0.44%) of Rab's real converted corpus carries a structure tree (docs/52, re-quoted not re-derived), and neither WTPDF nor ISO 32000-2 contains multi-column body pages in the specimens sampled — so this lane's negative result is solid on the specimens available but does not close the question for the algorithm's real niche. Did not attempt to run J24's actual marker_blocks.json output through xy_cut() (no J24-blocks book also carries a structure tree, so there's nothing to score it against) — confirmed this is a structural gap in the available ground truth, not a shortcut taken. Did not build the REDS-style graded metric (paragraph-boundary Levenshtein + Hungarian matching) — flagged IDEA_ONLY as a good next metric, zero lines written.

lanes.measured_on_specimen: Ran latex_balance (verbatim reimplementation of fidelity_audit.py:373-424, no pymupdf/rapidfuzz needed) against the actual held Damodaran 4e markdown (C:/Users/Bndit/ml/library/held/14c66834bdfeaa2e/...Four.md, 29,697 lines). Result: array env begin=87 end=84 unterminated=3 (not 61 as the commission's GROUND text asserted) - cross-checked against SYMPTOM-INDEX.md's own pre-existing SYM-056 row ("anchored Investment Valuation bundle...delta 3, already vaulted") which independently agrees on delta=3 via a differently-shaped literal-count method. The 61/60/40 figures belong to a different book (Ashby), quoted verbatim in that same SYMPTOM-INDEX row. Also measured: colspec width of all 87 array opens (max 3 columns, zero match Ashby's degenerate 36-column signature) and a markdown pipe-table/empty-cell census (4,580 table rows across 235 pages, 4,712 empty-cell markers across 217 pages - this is the real dense-financial-table data, top pages 805/564/757/779/579/888/1012). Negative control: latex_balance's other 4 LaTeX envs (align*, aligned, bmatrix, cases) do not uniformly read unterminated (aligned and cases show only stray closes, 0 unterminated) - the method discriminates rather than flagging everything. Second negative control: caught my own page-mapping artifact mid-measurement (a naive bucket wrongly absorbed 839 lines of front matter into "page 1" because the <span id="page-N-M"> anchors are image-adjacent, not one-per-page) and reported it as a stated limitation rather than silently trusting it. Also read marker's actual installed table processor (marker-env/Lib/site-packages/marker/processors/table.py) confirming it already imports surya.table_rec.TableRecPredictor and combines it with pdftext glyph-level extraction on non-OCR pages - grounding what "glyph geometry" already does and doesn't cover in the running pipeline.
